content.body: Hoping to have my thoughts on it actually worked through by the plenary

Having written a decent amount of code that cares about reasoning when it will can be re-entered, I would really like to have a way to "mark something as aborted" without opening myself to random code executing at that point. That's my concern with a synchronous notification system.

There is possibly an argument to be made that's a behavior the code that creates / owns the controller get to chose.
If that function doesn't want the callback to be re-entrant then what should it do? Should it `Promise.resolve().then(() => cb(nextItem))`, or should it put a guard at the top (probably this)

function process(data) {
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const source = new Source({ signal: ac.signal });
    while (looping) {
         if (getSomething()) {
              ac.abort();
              break;
         }
    }
}

content.body: Then same for this ^^, if it doesn't want `.ac.abort()` to be re-entrant what should it do? Feels better to add a guard than rely on the notification being delivered async.
content.formatted_body: Then same for this ^^, if it doesn't want .ac.abort() to be re-entrant what should it do? Feels better to add a guard than rely on the notification being delivered async.

And in practice I don't see code like the above, usually the abort is one of these two patterns:

process.on('SIGINT', () => {
  ac.abort(); // no-re-entrancy risk here
});

or

try {
   ...
} finally {
   ac.abort(); // we've already finished on our side, just letting everyone else know
}
